assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors convert a programmable DNA-binding step into a defined deaminase chemistry on a single base, without double-strand breaks. This is a clean chemical-mechanism story with a general tool for biologists and direct therapeutic reach; from my genome-maintenance view the avoidance of break-driven repair is conceptually important.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory conceived and led both editor classes; Komor developed the first cytosine base editors and Gaudelli the adenine base editors (which required evolving a deaminase for DNA). Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work is real but later in the supplied credit; a fair prize could be Liu with Komor and Gaudelli or Liu alone, with the Kondo/Nishida question unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced across many labs and cell types, with clinical trials under way, so the technology is validated. Clinical outcome data are still emerging, which argues somewhat for patience but not against recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prime-editing candidate and with CRISPR already honored (2020) may make the committee prefer one combined or one separate award.
Attribution of Target-AID (Kondo, Nishida) versus Liu's group priority is disputed in emphasis; I cannot verify exact dates.
Long-term off-target deamination and clinical safety evidence remain incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system turns a biological pathway into a drug-design chemistry: heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues such as thalidomide analogues. It changes the definition of druggable target and has a mechanistic chemical basis I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the first PROTAC concept; Ciulli delivered key structure-based VHL ligand chemistry and ternary-complex mechanism. Handa, Ito and others clarified cereblon as the thalidomide target and Sakamoto contributed early peptide PROTAC work, so a three-person prize leaves out several credible contributors and the glue branch.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials and the principle is reproduced widely, but approvals are still pending, so confirmation of therapeutic payoff is incomplete although the mechanism is solid.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: PROTACs and molecular glues (cereblon) may need different recognition.
No approved PROTAC drug yet, so clinical maturity could be considered premature.
Credit among Sakamoto, Crews, Deshaies and Handa/Ito is contested in emphasis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible methylation of mRNA adenosine, with writers, erasers (FTO, ALKBH5) and readers, defines a chemical regulatory layer on RNA. It is a clear chemical-modification discovery with broad biological consequence in development, cancer and metabolism.
assessment.attribution: He proposed and demonstrated reversibility (FTO as an m6A demethylase) and led the field; Jaffrey and Rechavi with Dominissini mapped m6A transcriptome-wide in 2012. Dominissini and Meyer did key mapping work, so credit is split between concept and mapping.
assessment.maturity: Heavily replicated in concept, but quantitative stoichiometry and some functional claims remain debated, and some mapping methods have shown artifacts. I would want measurements validated with orthogonal quantification.
uncertainties: Debate on whether FTO acts on m6A or m6Am and on site-level stoichiometry and function.
Priority between mapping groups and the Chuan He demethylation discovery is unresolved.
Therapeutic payoff remains early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for membraneless compartments reframed cell organization, with a physical-chemical basis for condensates such as P granules and nucleoli. Its conceptual importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids in 2009; Rosen demonstrated multivalent-interaction phase separation in reconstituted systems; Pappu and Mittag developed the sequence-grammar theory. A three-person prize is plausible but leaves out Pappu and Mittag.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted, but as a measurement-minded biochemist I worry that many cellular claims of phase separation rest on overexpression and imaging; the concept is accepted while many specific cases need quantitative, in vivo testing.
uncertainties: Controversy about which cellular condensates are truly liquid and functionally relevant at endogenous concentrations.
Whether the discovery is a chemistry rather than a cell-biology award.
Allocation among five credited people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides and polony clusters made large-scale sequencing cheap and general, which underpins genomics and medicine. The chemistry of reversible terminators and fluorophore cleavage is specific and elegant.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the approach and Mayer co-developed clustered amplification (Manteia). Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454) and Ju are also credited, so the configuration of the prize is complicated by competing technologies.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly proven: dominant platform for nearly two decades. Timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with Sanger sequencing (1980) recognition and credit division with Rothberg, Ju and Mayer.
Whether the committee views this as chemistry or as genomics technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemical genetics with analog-sensitive kinases and covalent targeting of KRAS G12C through the switch-II pocket cysteine broke the long-held view that RAS was undruggable. It is a chemical principle with direct patient benefit (sotorasib, adagrasib).
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the single clear originator of both threads; credit is unusually clean, though the clinical molecules were developed by industry teams building on his work.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated with approved drugs and independently reproduced, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Compound discovery of two themes: kinase chemical genetics and covalent KRAS inhibitors.
A one-person prize versus a broader covalent-drugging prize with industry contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids in living cells, turning protein translation into programmable chemistry for biologists. A general and widely used tool.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo genetic code expansion in E. coli and yeast; Chin extended it to eukaryotes and to quadruplet and reassigned codons, with Mehl and Yokoyama contributing technical advances. Schultz with Chin and Wang is a reasonable configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and used for decades; applications such as engineered therapeutics continue to appear. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Relative credit among Schultz, Wang and Chin.
Breadth of impact beyond specialist laboratories is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structure and mechanism of nitrogenase, the enzyme that reduces N2 to ammonia, is a fundamental biological chemistry problem. The FeMo-cofactor structure with its central carbide and the turnover intermediates reveal the mechanism, which I find compelling as enzymology.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle solved the FeMo-cofactor structure and the central carbide; Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe contributed mechanistic and biosynthetic work. Attribution among five names is difficult and I am uncertain how the committee would divide it.
assessment.maturity: Structure is well established, but the exact N2-binding mechanism and substrate-binding site remain under study, so the mechanism is not fully settled.
uncertainties: The catalytic mechanism is incompletely resolved.
Credit among structural, spectroscopic and biochemical groups is unclear.
Haber-Bosch recognition (1918, 1931) and prior nitrogenase-related work may affect appetite for this prize.
